title: failed writer-record publication still authorizes dropping the last protection
mechanism_summary: SDK completion and the grace callback swallow a rejected recordWriter promise and call dropWorkspaceLease anyway, so an ENOSPC at the writer-record write leaves no record, no lease and a deleted workspace, and the abandoned handler's late write gets ENOENT.

finder_sections.text:
### 1. P1 — failed publication still authorizes dropping the last protection

[SDK completion](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/bf2505618f52/packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts#L4571-L4582) catches a rejected `recordWriter` promise and calls `dropWorkspaceLease` anyway. [Grace](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/bf2505618f52/packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts#L4604-L4610) does the same through `catch(...).finally(dropWorkspaceLease)`. Awaiting a promise whose failure has been swallowed is not a successful publication barrier.

Injected ENOSPC only at the real writer-record atomic write. Real SDK shutdown, its real two-second abandonment, real leases and real cleanup were not replaced. Result: one publication failure, no record, no lease, one capture, workspace absent; resuming the actual handler produces ENOENT. The real 30-second grace reproduces the same loss for a blocked flush writer. The successful-publication control at **30,004 ms** keeps one record, preserves the late write, and captures once after completion. [Probe](r17-writers-ordered.test.ts), [full log](writers-ordered.log).

Correction needed: failure to publish must preserve an effective protection, rather than mean that the session may release it. This alone keeps the head in draft.

real_because.quote: | Carried P1: rejected publication drops protection | **CLOSED for the reported completion and grace failures.** | The unchanged reproduction now reports `record:false, lease:true, present:true, failures:6, captures:0`; the late write succeeds.

title: release-capture retention renames a live workspace out from under its recorded writer
mechanism_summary: retainIsolationWorkspace renames the base directory on patch failure without asking about leases or unfinished writers, so a live writer record travels into the .retained-* copy and the writer's next write at its original cwd gets ENOENT.

finder_sections.text:
### 2. P1 — release-capture retention bypasses the writer barrier by renaming the live workspace

[The release capture](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/bf2505618f52/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-runner.ts#L438-L457) handles patch failure by calling [retainIsolationWorkspace](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/bf2505618f52/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-runner.ts#L319-L344). That helper renames the base directory without asking about leases or unfinished writers. Protecting only deletion is insufficient: the writer uses its original cwd pathname.

Actual isolated runner + real SDK shutdown handler, with successful record publication. Only the release-time patch write is made to fail with ENOSPC. The caller's release runs once, but the workspace moves to `.retained-*` with a **live writer record still inside it**. The abandoned handler then writes `late-save` at its original cwd and gets ENOENT. Observed: `abandoned:true, workspace:false, baseReleases:1, failed:1, writer:true`. [Probe](r17-retain-writer.test.ts), [log](retention-writer.log).

The source was retained, not deleted; the **new late write was lost**. Unique allocation already removes the original reason given in this helper's stale comment for moving a retained workspace out of a deterministic slot. Retention must not invalidate a path still used by a protected writer.

real_because.quote: | Retention renames a workspace beneath its recorded writer | **OPEN as a class. The exact recorded-writer reproduction is fixed.** | The original runner reproduction now writes successfully at its original cwd.

title: ordinary reclamation hands a freed sandbox name back out and a surviving git hook reads its successor's tree
mechanism_summary: Exclusive mkdir only answers whether the name exists now, so after an ordinary `worktree clear` frees a dead owner's sandbox the same inputs mint the same path again and a still-running reference-transaction hook from the dead run lists the successor's files.

finder_sections.text:
### 3. P2 — ordinary reclamation reopens the same surviving-hook pathname attack

[Exclusive mkdir](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/bf2505618f52/packages/coding-agent/src/task/worktree.ts#L659-L673) answers whether the name exists **now**, not whether it has ever been handed out. Successful cleanup and ordinary reclamation remove that evidence.

Three distinct observations:

1. Two fresh processes with identical clock/entropy inputs, unmodified `Snowflake.next` and unmodified `ensureIsolation`: while allocation one exists, allocation two skips it; both outputs survive. **This original collision case is repaired.**
2. Insert ordinary `clearWorktrees({json:true})` after the first process exits. It removes one sandbox. With the same inputs, process two obtains exactly the first pathname. [Controlled default-generator result](restored-reclaimed.log). This is a restored-input experiment, not a claimed naturally observed wall-clock collision.
3. Real `cleanupIsolation -> commitToBranch -> git fetch -> reference-transaction` hook. Kill and await the exact capture owner; its hook remains. Ordinary clear removes the dead owner's sandbox. Force the materialisation mint to repeat, allocate its now-free name, and write `second-only`. The actual surviving hook reads `["tracked", ".git", "second-only"]`. [Hook result](hook-reclaimed.log). No `--all` or deletion of a live owner was required. A one-collision-then-fresh-name control keeps the old hook away from the successor: [control](hook-occupied.log).

The kernel correctly prevents simultaneous occupancy. The advertised assumption-free **never-handed-out-again** guarantee, and its surviving-descendant consequence, remain false after reclamation.

real_because.quote: | Reclamation allows deterministic remint and a surviving Git hook reads its successor | **CLOSED for the reported vulnerability.** | Ordinary clear removes the first sandbox. Identical clock and Snowflake seed inputs then produce different paths. The surviving real hook sees ENOENT at the old path, not `second-only`.

title: the new unref never reaches the real filesystem watchers because the wrapper exposes only close
mechanism_summary: watchLeaseDirectory returns a cast wrapper carrying only `close`, so `workspace.watcher?.unref?.()` silently does nothing and a plain program that has finished its work still cannot exit.

finder_sections.text:
### 4. P2 — the new unref does not reach the real filesystem watchers

[The call](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/bf2505618f52/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts#L394-L400) invokes `workspace.watcher?.unref?.()`. [watchLeaseDirectory](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/bf2505618f52/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts#L327-L348) returns a cast wrapper containing **only `close`**, not `unref`. Optional chaining silently does nothing; the underlying lease/writer watchers stay referenced.

A plain `bun program.ts` completes disposal and the actual abandoned handler's final write, closes auth storage, disconnects IPC and reaches end-of-source. It still does not exit; the exact child must be killed and awaited. Ordinary 10-ms non-timeout control exits naturally with **code 0**. Making watch unavailable in a separate corrected control permits the 2.5-second abandoned-handler case to exit naturally with **code 0**, proving that unref of the poll alone works. [Normal/kept observations](natural-exit.log), [corrected no-watch control](natural-no-watch.log), [plain source](r17-natural-writer.ts).

real_because.quote: | The watch wrapper drops `unref` | **CLOSED.** | All three plain-program controls exit naturally with code 0: ordinary disposal, abandoned shutdown with watches, and abandoned shutdown without watches. Instrumented real watchers receive two `unref` calls and ten `ref` calls during a writer handoff.

title: the same unref abandons a foreign writer's final capture when fs.watch is unavailable
mechanism_summary: The unfinished-writer branch unrefs the polling fallback no matter which process the record names, so the owner exits code 0 before a foreign writer finishes and the final capture never runs.

finder_sections.text:
### 5. P2 — unref also abandons a foreign writer's final capture when watching is unavailable

The same [unfinished-writer branch](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/bf2505618f52/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts#L394-L400) unrefs regardless of which process the record names. A foreign writer's exit is not a condition requiring the **owner** process to exit.

Real owner and writer Bun processes. The foreign process publishes a real writer record. Injected watch-limit ENOSPC selects the existing polling fallback; no process exit or timer is mocked. Owner cleanup defers capture, then the owner's unreferenced poll allows natural **code-0 exit before the foreign writer finishes**. The writer subsequently writes and clears its record, also exits 0, but the capture callback died with its owner: `captured:false`, while source contains `last foreign write`. [Probe](r17-foreign-unref.test.ts), [owner](r17-foreign-owner.ts), [log](foreign-unref.log).

This loses automatic final capture, not the retained source file. Forwarding the missing watcher `unref` alone would expose this case even when watch succeeds. Distinguish a self-owned process-lifetime record from a foreign writer whose departure the owner must still observe.

real_because.quote: | Unreferenced waiting loses a foreign writer's final capture | **OPEN as a class. The ordinary foreign-record case is fixed.** | Both watched and polling owners now wait, capture, and exit 0.

title: descriptor exhaustion is reported as proof that nothing holds the workspace
mechanism_summary: The EMFILE branch prints 'Nothing is holding the workspace' when it could not open the lock at all, so a real native holder in the same process is reported as no holder, and the native errno is replaced by (GenericFailure).

finder_sections.text:
### 7. P2 — diagnostics still make an unsupported holder claim

The actual EMFILE branch now fires immediately, but [its text](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/bf2505618f52/packages/coding-agent/src/task/worktree.ts#L893-L901) infers “Nothing is holding the workspace” from descriptor exhaustion. A real native lock held in the same process disproves that assertion. EMFILE prevents discovery; it does not establish absence of a holder. The output also displays `(GenericFailure)` rather than the native errno. Lease and forced-clear retain raw native errors without holder identity. [Real matrix](descriptor-matrix.log).

real_because.quote: The real descriptor-exhaustion matrix opens 240 descriptors under `prlimit --nofile=256:256`. A real native holder exists. Cleanup now correctly says the lock could not be opened and holder status is unknown. It no longer claims nothing holds the workspace.

title: the 64-collision mint bound hides EEXIST from every caller-visible message
mechanism_summary: At the mint's 64-collision bound the thrown error keeps EEXIST only in `.cause`, and the structured failure formatter copies `.message` into stderr and error, so the caller never learns which failure exhausted the bound.

finder_sections.text:
### 8. P3 — collision-bound exhaustion hides its last failure from the caller

At the 64-collision bound, `.cause.code` is EEXIST, but the thrown message contains only “Could not mint an unused isolation workspace under …”. The real [structured failure formatter](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/bf2505618f52/packages/coding-agent/src/task/structured-subagent.ts#L740-L759) copies `.message` into both `stderr` and `error`, losing the cause. This fails the requested caller-visible explanation of which failure exhausted the bound. [Bound evidence](allocation.log).

Non-EEXIST refusal is otherwise correct: real mkdir EACCES is surfaced; a real overlong-name error is surfaced from the preceding realpath; injected candidate-mkdir EACCES, ENOSPC, ENAMETOOLONG and EROFS each propagate after **one** attempt. Trying `/sys` under this user yielded EACCES before any EROFS condition; it is not represented as a real EROFS reproduction. No shared filesystem was filled or remounted. [Propagation matrix](mkdir-errno.log).

real_because.quote: | Mint exhaustion hides EEXIST from the caller | **CLOSED.** | Real mkdir collisions consume exactly 64 attempts. The message includes both `64` and `EEXIST`, plus the last error.

title: completion still drops the lease after publication fails, and the retry awaits the same rejected promise
mechanism_summary: The completion callback catches a publication failure and calls dropWorkspaceLease anyway, and recordWriter keeps the rejected promise so the grace loop re-awaits that rejection instead of publishing again.

finder_sections.text:
### 1. P1 — completion still drops the lease after publication fails

This is the carried data-loss finding, not a new speculative case.

The [completion callback](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/04d7827218fb/packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts#L4586-L4596) still catches publication failure and then calls `dropWorkspaceLease()`. The new retry protects only the grace callback.

I injected ENOSPC only at the real writer-record write. The actual SDK abandoned its shutdown handler at its normal deadline. Disposal returned with:

```text
record:false, lease:false, present:false, failures:1, captures:1
late write: ENOENT
```

The exact round-seventeen reproduction still fails. A separate one-failure-only probe also loses the late write, although the storage fault is then gone. [Original reproduction](initial-publication.log), [independent transient case](publication-boundaries.log), [probe](r18-publication.test.ts).

There is a second defect in the claimed retry. [`recordWriter`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/04d7827218fb/packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts#L4512-L4515) retains the rejected promise. The grace loop repeatedly awaits that rejection instead of calling `markUnfinishedWriter` again. With access restored before grace, the observed write count remains **one** at 32 seconds. There is no record and the lease remains held.

The grace-specific protection itself works. An always-rejecting publication leaves the lease and source intact at 31.5 seconds. A publication that rejects after grace also leaves both intact at 33 seconds. Successful publication held pending for 31.5 seconds preserves the lease, then produces one mark, one clear, and one capture after its gate opens. [Failure matrix](publication-boundaries.log), [pending-success replay](history-r17-generation.test.log).

**Required correction:** preserve effective protection on every failed-publication path. A retry must perform a new publication attempt, not await the same rejected promise.

real_because.quote: | Carried P1: rejected publication drops protection | **CLOSED for the reported completion and grace failures.** | The unchanged reproduction now reports `record:false, lease:true, present:true, failures:6, captures:0`; the late write succeeds. The transient case makes two actual writes and keeps a record.

title: retention renames a workspace another live SDK session is leasing
mechanism_summary: The new pre-rename check consults unfinished-writer records only; it never looks at leases and never serializes the check and the rename with lease admission, so a second live SDK session's cwd is renamed away and its next write gets ENOENT.

finder_sections.text:
### 2. P1 — retention still renames a workspace used by another live session

The [new check](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/04d7827218fb/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-runner.ts#L323-L350) checks unfinished-writer records only. It neither checks leases nor serializes the check and rename with admission.

Actual isolated runner, actual second SDK session, actual live lease. I injected ENOSPC only when the owner writes its release patch. The owner then retained the workspace by renaming it:

```text
releases:1, failures:1, otherDisposed:false
retained directory: lease:true, writer:false
other session's next write: ENOENT
```

[Integration evidence](retain-live-session.log), [probe](r18-retain-live-session.test.ts).

Two controlled races also fail. Clearing one writer record while another lease remains permits the rename. Publishing a record immediately before the rename moves that live record and invalidates its cwd. Both late writes return ENOENT. [Race evidence](retention-boundaries.log).

**Required correction:** retention must preserve every active user's pathname, not only records visible at one unlocked check. The original recorded-writer case passes, but the protection class remains incomplete.

real_because.quote: | Retention moves another live session's workspace | **OPEN.** | The original already-open second SDK session now keeps its cwd.

title: in-place retention reports sidecarOk true before the code that writes the backend sidecar
mechanism_summary: The in-place early return answers sidecarOk:true ahead of the retained-backend sidecar write, so Overlayfs, Btrfs and Projfs workspaces are retained with no metadata and native stop is never dispatched.

finder_sections.text:
### 3. P2 — in-place retention reports valid native metadata without writing it

The [early return](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/04d7827218fb/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-runner.ts#L329-L344) returns `sidecarOk:true` before the code that writes the retained-backend sidecar.

For Overlayfs, Btrfs, and Projfs, the probe observes the same result:

```text
sidecarOk:true, metadata:null, stops:0
ordinary clear: removed:1, failed:0
```

The test uses real directories and the actual retention/clear code. It supplies each native backend kind and spies on native stop. It does not mount those filesystems. [Evidence](retention-boundaries.log), [probe](r18-retention.test.ts).

The measured defect is missing metadata and skipped backend dispatch. [INFERENCE] On an actual mounted or subvolume-backed workspace, clear can traverse the view or fail to remove its backing resource. The [clear implementation](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/04d7827218fb/packages/coding-agent/src/cli/worktree-cli.ts#L76-L100) requires the sidecar before native stop. Its existing comment explains why recursive removal is not a substitute.

**Required correction:** preserve required teardown metadata on the in-place path too. Report metadata failure truthfully.

real_because.quote: | In-place retention omits native teardown metadata | **CLOSED.** | Overlayfs, Btrfs, and Projfs each record the correct backend and invoke native-stop dispatch once. Injected sidecar failures return `sidecarOk:false`.

title: a later foreign lease does not re-reference an already unreferenced wait
mechanism_summary: settleIfIdle returns as soon as a lease exists, ahead of both ref calls, so an owner that already unref'd its watchers for its own record never re-refs when a second process takes a lease, and exits before the foreign write.

finder_sections.text:
### 4. P2 — a later foreign lease does not re-reference an already unreferenced wait

[`settleIfIdle`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/04d7827218fb/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts#L415-L431) returns immediately when a lease exists. That return precedes both `ref` calls.

The owner first waits on its own writer record. Its actual watchers receive two `unref` calls. A second process then acquires a real lease, and the owner clears its own record. The lease path never restores references:

```text
unrefs:2, refs:0
prematurelyExited:true, ownerCode:0, writerCode:0
captured:false, lateSource:"last foreign write"
```

The same handoff to a foreign writer **record** succeeds: `refs:10`, final capture runs, and both processes exit 0. [Evidence](exit-boundaries.log), [owner probe](r18-foreign-owner.ts), [test](r18-exit.test.ts).

**Required correction:** when any foreign work still requires this owner's capture, restore the references before returning. This defect loses automatic final capture, not the retained source file.

real_because.quote: | Later foreign lease fails to restore references | **CLOSED.** | The unchanged case reports `unrefs:2, refs:16`, no premature exit, final capture, and owner exit 0.

mechanism: returns immediately when a lease exists

title: an unreadable writer directory is counted as proof that every writer is this process's own
mechanism_summary: ownsEveryUnfinishedWriter turns every readdir failure into an empty list and then returns true, reversing the conservative answer the preceding check gave for the same EACCES and unreferencing the wait.

finder_sections.text:
### 5. P2 — an unreadable writer directory is treated as exclusively self-owned

[`ownsEveryUnfinishedWriter`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/04d7827218fb/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts#L309-L317) converts every readdir failure into an empty list. It then returns true.

The preceding check correctly treats that same error as an unfinished writer. The ownership check reverses that conservative decision and unreferences the wait.

I injected EACCES only for the owner's writer-directory listing. A real foreign writer and record remained live. The owner exited naturally with code 0 before the foreign write. The writer later succeeded, but `captured:false`. [Evidence](exit-boundaries.log).

**Required correction:** unknown ownership must not count as proof that every writer belongs to this process.

real_because.quote: | EACCES listing writers is treated as self-owned absence | **CLOSED.** | The unchanged fault no longer permits early exit. With access subsequently restored, capture completes and the owner exits 0.

title: slow clear retries start every five seconds without waiting for the previous call
mechanism_summary: The clear retry interval fires another clear() on every tick regardless of whether the last one has settled, so a stalled clear accumulates concurrent in-flight operations.

finder_sections.text:
### 6. P2 — slow clear retries overlap without a bound

The [new interval](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/04d7827218fb/packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts#L4539-L4549) starts another `clear()` every five seconds without waiting for the previous call.

After the first five failures, I held each slow clear pending at the filesystem boundary. The probe records:

```text
calls:8, maxInflight:3
attempt times in ms: 0, 200, 401, 601, 802, 6003, 11003, 16004
```

No completion occurred between the last three calls. [Evidence](publication-boundaries.log).

This is not a hot retry loop. Always-rejecting calls remain five seconds apart. The defect is unbounded concurrent work when a clear stalls. The source starts another pending operation on every tick.

Recovery and process-exit controls pass. Restoring access produces exactly six calls, one capture, and no record. Repeated disposal creates no extra clear. A plain program exits naturally with code 0 after five failed fast clears, despite the pending slow timer. [Recovery](publication-boundaries.log), [plain exit](exit-boundaries.log).

**Required correction:** allow only one slow clear in flight. Preserve the unreferenced wait and successful-recovery behavior.

real_because.quote: | Slow clear retries overlap without a bound | **CLOSED.** | A held slow clear produces six total calls, `maxInflight:1`, rather than three concurrent slow calls.

title: an unreadable owner marker is converted to 'no sandbox', so lease and publication succeed as no-ops
mechanism_summary: Sandbox discovery recognises only `claimed` and `retiring`, so an `unknown` claim from a real EACCES on the marker falls through and returns undefined, and both lease admission and writer publication return a successful no-op release while the workspace is then deleted.

finder_sections.text:
### R19-1 — P1: an unreadable owner marker is still converted to “no sandbox,” so publication can succeed without a record

[Sandbox discovery](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/50695fad4206/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts#L128-L142) recognizes only `claimed` and `retiring`. An `unknown` claim, including a real EACCES, falls through the walk and returns undefined. Both [lease admission](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/50695fad4206/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts#L224-L231) and [writer publication](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/50695fad4206/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts#L269-L275) then return a successful no-op release/clear.

The filesystem fault is real: chmod the existing owner marker to mode 000, call the actual discovery/publication code, then restore mode 0600 before cleanup. Direct lease admission returns a release function with no error and no recorded lease. In the actual SDK shutdown path, the no-op publication is cached as success. Disposal abandons its handler, drops the real lease, and cleanup deletes the workspace:

```text
claim.kind: unknown; reason: EACCES
publication calls: 1
record:false, lease:false, present:false, captures:1
late write: ENOENT
```

This is the requested third failure-as-absence path. The retry memo cannot repair it because nothing rejects. The cleanup barrier matters: the first diagnostic probe observed the gap after lease removal but before teardown, and its immediate late write succeeded. The corrected probe re-enters actual serialized cleanup before releasing the writer; it reproduces the loss without a guessed delay.

[Probe](r19-absence.test.ts) · [Evidence](absence-with-teardown-barrier.log). **Required correction:** unknown sandbox ownership must not be returned as a successful absence/no-op at either admission or publication.

real_because.quote: | P1 unknown marker treated as absent | **OPEN for an existing dangling marker; CLOSED for EACCES, EIO, ELOOP, empty, directory and partial JSON.** The unchanged direct EACCES admission test passes with an error and no lease, and the adjusted real shutdown retains lease and late write.

title: retention still has an admission and publication window between its check and its rename
mechanism_summary: The check and the rename are not one protected operation on the unlocked release-capture path, so a second SDK session admitted through the ordinary lease API after the check has its cwd renamed away.

finder_sections.text:
### R19-2 — P1: retention still has an admission/publication window between its check and rename

The [checks](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/50695fad4206/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-runner.ts#L323-L342) and [rename](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/50695fad4206/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-runner.ts#L344-L363) are not one protected operation on the unlocked release-capture path.

I gated the actual base-directory rename, admitted an actual second SDK session through the normal lease API, and then let rename proceed. This is a real isolated runner with ENOSPC injected only at patch storage:

```text
renames:1, leaseBeforeRename:true, otherDisposed:false
next write at the second session's cwd: ENOENT
```

The opposite ordering is safe: releasing the last lease immediately before the check permits the move and preserves the original file in the retained directory. The already-open-session regression is fixed. But the unchanged writer-publication race still moves a newly recorded writer and gives its late write ENOENT.

[Boundary probes](r19-retention.test.ts) · [Evidence](retention-ordering.log) · [Publication race](history-r18-retention.test.log). **Required correction:** preserve active users' pathname throughout retention, including admission and publication between the look and move—not just users visible in the first snapshot.

real_because.quote: | P1 check-then-act retention | **OPEN for writer publication; CLOSED for lease admission.** The unchanged second-SDK-session test itself times out because its `fs.rename` spy waits *inside* the held rename for admission to complete

title: the final foreign writer can disappear between the presence check and the ownership listing
mechanism_summary: hasUnfinishedWriter followed by ownsEveryUnfinishedWriter is not one snapshot: an empty second listing reads as 'all remaining writers are ours', so the owner unrefs the poll and returns instead of taking the capture that has just become due.

finder_sections.text:
### R19-3 — P2: the final foreign writer can disappear between two reads, causing the owner to exit without final capture

[`hasUnfinishedWriter` followed by `ownsEveryUnfinishedWriter`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/50695fad4206/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts#L434-L450) is not a stable snapshot. [An empty second directory listing](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/50695fad4206/packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts#L312-L328) returns true: “all remaining writers are ours.” It then unreferences the poll and returns instead of performing the now-due capture.

With fs.watch unavailable, a real foreign writer writes its output and clears its record between the first presence check and the ownership listing. The boundary gate takes 12.46 ms, less than the next poll period. Both processes exit normally:

```text
ownership entries: []
ownerCode:0, writerCode:0
captured:false, source:"last foreign write"
```

Files: `packages/coding-agent/src/cli/worktree-cli.ts:369-394,399-403,281`.

`scanWorktrees` adds an unreadable child with `keep:true`, but does not count that child as a reason to preserve its parent. It then adds the parent as an unrecognized stray. Default clear skips the child and recursively deletes its parent, including the child's content.

- `r24-boundaries-current.log:11,42`: ordinary scan preserves a live nested sandbox. Child-stat `EACCES` produces `removed:1,present:false`, despite `keep:true` on that child.
- `r24-pr-unknown.log:12,43`: a real linked Git worktree with uncommitted content is preserved normally. `EIO` at its `.git` stat makes the checkout a stray. Default clear deletes its uncommitted file.

This is a concrete `unknown`-to-unprotected boundary. The union survives the lookup, but the parent aggregation discards its protection. The older catch-all at `classifyDir` also collapses a `.git` lookup failure to null.

## 1. P1 — the capture returns the empty patch, and the teardown deletes the only copy, when a directory in the sandbox cannot be listed

This is the defect this pull request exists to close, on the current head: a
read fails, the failure becomes "nothing is there", and the absence authorises

the empty patch that deleted a user's file" — does not cover it.

`captureRepoDeltaPatch` (`worktree.ts:461`) asks git for the untracked set:

```ts
const currentUntracked = await repo.lsFiles(true, true);
const currentUntracked_ = await captureUntrackedPatch(repoDir, currentUntracked, repo);
if (currentUntracked_.unread.length > 0) { throw new IsolationCaptureIncompleteError(...) }
```

cannot name a file git never listed. `git ls-files --others` skips a directory
it cannot open, writes `warning: could not open directory 'locked/'` to stderr
and **exits 0**; `lsFiles` has no error channel (`packages/natives/native/index.d.ts:749`
— `lsFiles(others, excludeStandard, signal?): Promise<Array<string>>`), so the
short listing arrives as a complete one.
